title: 寻隐者不遇
title_en: Looking for the Hermit and Not Finding Him
author: 贾岛

text_note.zh: 资料库把这首诗题作《访羊尊师》，作者记为孙革。通行本和课本题作《寻隐者不遇》，作者贾岛。
text_note.en: The corpus titles this poem "Visiting Master Yang" and gives the author as Sun Ge. The common version and textbooks title it "Looking for the Hermit and Not Finding Him", by Jia Dao.

readings.zh: 童子就是小孩子，课本读 tóng zǐ，子读第三声。
readings.en: Tóng zǐ means a young boy; textbooks read this character zǐ, third tone.

readings.zh: 只是“只是、就”的意思，读 zhǐ。
readings.en: Here it means "only, just", read zhǐ.

glosses.zh: 童子：小孩子，这里指隐者的小徒弟。
glosses.en: tóng zǐ: a young boy; here, the hermit's young pupil.
cǎi yào: to gather medicinal herbs in the mountains.
yún shēn: the clouds are thick.

glosses.zh: 不知处：不知道他在哪里。
glosses.en: bù zhī chù: no one knows where he is.

translation.zh: 我在松树下问隐者的小徒弟，
translation.en: Under the pine tree, I ask the hermit's young pupil.

translation.zh: 他说：师父去山里采药了。
translation.en: He says: My master has gone to gather herbs.
He is somewhere on this mountain,

translation.zh: 可是云雾太浓，不知道他在哪儿。
translation.en: but the clouds are so thick, I can't tell where.

background.zh: 隐者就是不愿做官、住在深山里的人。这首诗写诗人去山里拜访一位隐者，却没有见到他。写作年份不清楚，隐者是谁也不知道。这首诗在有的古书里题作《访羊尊师》，作者记为孙革，但通行的说法和课本都认为是贾岛写的。
background.en: A hermit is someone who does not want to be an official and lives deep in the mountains. In this poem the poet goes to the mountains to visit a hermit but does not find him. The year it was written is not known, and neither is the hermit's name. Some old books title it "Visiting Master Yang" and give the author as Sun Ge, but the common view, and textbooks, hold that it is by Jia Dao.

author_note.zh: 贾岛（779—843），中唐诗人。他年轻时当过和尚，后来还俗，去考进士。他写诗特别用心，一个字要想很久。有个故事说，他为“僧推月下门”还是“僧敲月下门”拿不定主意，在路上想得入迷，撞到了韩愈的车队。“推敲”这个词就是这么来的。
author_note.en: Jia Dao (779–843) was a poet of the middle Tang. As a young man he was a Buddhist monk, then returned to ordinary life to sit the civil service exams. He worked very hard on his poems and would think about a single word for a long time. One story says he could not decide between "the monk pushes the gate under the moon" and "the monk knocks on the gate under the moon". Lost in thought on the road, he bumped into the procession of the official Han Yu. The Chinese word for "weighing your words", tuī qiāo, comes from this story.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗只有二十个字，却藏着一问三答。诗人问了什么，诗里没写，可我们从小徒弟的回答里都能猜出来：“你师父呢？”“采药去了。”“在哪儿采？”“就在这山里。”“具体在哪儿？”“云太深，不知道。”问答一步一步，诗人的心情也跟着变：先是失望，又有了希望，最后又落空了。松树、白云、深山，也让我们看到隐者的生活多么清静、自在。没见到人，却好像已经见到了他的样子。
appreciation.en: This poem has only twenty characters, yet it hides one question and three answers. The poem does not write the poet's questions, but we can guess them from the boy's replies. "Where is your master?" "Gone to gather herbs." "Where?" "Somewhere on this mountain." "Where exactly?" "The clouds are too thick, I don't know." Step by step, the poet's feelings change: first disappointment, then hope, and at last hope slips away again. The pine, the white clouds and the deep mountain also show us how calm and free the hermit's life is. We never meet him, yet it feels as if we have seen what he is like.
